title: Mark 12 External Feed Feasibility, Governance, and Build-Reliability Audit

inspectionFindings.networkCallsInSrc: None found — repository-wide search for fetch(, XMLHttpRequest, process.env found no matches. Only import.meta.env.PUBLIC_PREVIEW (a build-time static string flag) is read anywhere.

alternatives.name: Static manual curation
alternatives.requires: An owner-supplied evidence bundle per item/destination; a local content-collection record; a component update only if a new record shape is needed
alternatives.trustBoundaryDataCrossing: None — data originates locally, authored by a human, never fetched
alternatives.deploymentFragility: None added — identical to today's fully offline-capable build
alternatives.canFailBuild: Only via a normal schema-validation failure, never a network condition
alternatives.previewReproducibility: Full — output is deterministic from committed source
alternatives.staleContentRisk: Present but transparent — no illusion of freshness
alternatives.sourceMetadataExposureRisk: Minimal — only what a human deliberately transcribes
alternatives.appropriateForFounderSiteLater: Yes, pending that repository's own review (not performed here)

alternatives.name: Build-time network fetch
alternatives.requires: A build-time HTTP client, a documented source URL, a fallback/cache/timeout policy, a decision on preview vs production fetch behavior
alternatives.trustBoundaryDataCrossing: Yes — the build environment reaches out to a third-party host and trusts its response, subject to parsing/sanitization
alternatives.secretsNeeded: Not necessarily for a public feed; unresolved for GitHub
alternatives.deploymentFragility: Yes — a build now depends on a third party's uptime, response shape, and reachability
alternatives.canFailBuild: Yes, unless a fallback is proven to degrade gracefully (gate F5)
alternatives.previewReproducibility: At risk — two builds minutes apart could fetch different content
alternatives.staleContentRisk: Inverted from manual curation — can go stale silently unless failure is surfaced
alternatives.sourceMetadataExposureRisk: Higher — raw third-party response fields could carry more than intended unless explicitly filtered
alternatives.privacyPostureChange: Yes — introduces a category of third-party network dependency this repository has never had
alternatives.appropriateForFounderSiteLater: Only after a source-specific, owner-approved implementation request and full F0-F8 clearance in that repository

alternatives.name: Server-side/Worker proxy
alternatives.requires: Standing up a Cloudflare Worker or Pages Function, a deployment/runtime change, likely secret storage
alternatives.trustBoundaryDataCrossing: Yes, at runtime — a live request path between a visitor/edge and a third party
alternatives.secretsNeeded: Likely, especially for GitHub token-based rate-limit increases
alternatives.canFailBuild: Less likely to fail the build; shifts risk to runtime failures instead
alternatives.previewReproducibility: Compromised differently — could hit the same live proxy or diverge by environment
alternatives.staleContentRisk: Depends entirely on the proxy's own caching design
alternatives.sourceMetadataExposureRisk: Highest — a runtime proxy is a new attack surface and secret-leak risk
alternatives.privacyPostureChange: Significant — genuinely new infrastructure, not a content change
alternatives.appropriateForFounderSiteLater: Only as a last resort if build-time fetch proves infeasible, with its own dedicated infrastructure task; no Worker/adapter/Pages Function is configured anywhere in this repository today

alternatives.name: Scheduled ingestion with stored local content
alternatives.requires: A scheduled job, write access to the repository, a review/approval step before merge, same field-scoping/rights work as any individual item
alternatives.trustBoundaryDataCrossing: Yes, but only at the scheduled-job boundary — the build itself stays fully local/offline once content is committed
alternatives.secretsNeeded: Possibly, depending on source — same open GitHub-token question as B2
alternatives.deploymentFragility: Moderate — job failures don't affect the live site, but add new CI/automation surface
alternatives.canFailBuild: No, if designed correctly — a failed run produces no commit
alternatives.previewReproducibility: Preserved — every build from a committed commit is identical
alternatives.staleContentRisk: Present but bounded and visible — last-commit date is the freshness signal
alternatives.sourceMetadataExposureRisk: Same as B2 — ingestion step still needs field filtering before commit
alternatives.privacyPostureChange: Moderate — new automation surface, but live-site build behavior stays simple
alternatives.appropriateForFounderSiteLater: Possibly the strongest automated option if ever pursued — preserves build reliability better than B2/B3 — but requires its own dedicated task; no such job is configured today

alternatives.name: No feed / source-destination-only index
alternatives.requires: Nothing further — this is what exists today
alternatives.canFailBuild: No, for feed-related reasons — schema validation only, as always
alternatives.staleContentRisk: None in the silently-wrong sense — only a static outbound link exists
alternatives.sourceMetadataExposureRisk: Minimal — matches the already-audited Mark 10/11 model

partB_architectureAlternatives.defaultRecommendation: Manual curation (B1), or its zero-item variant (B5), remains the recommended current model for all four proposed sources. A build-time feed proof of concept (B2) may be considered later only after one real item has cleared G-M1 through G-M8 and only with a source-specific, owner-approved implementation request. No automatic model (B2, B3, or B4) is recommended for immediate implementation.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Owner source authorization
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Confirms the owner has explicitly proposed/authorized considering this specific external source as a future technical (not just source-destination) input, distinct from and prior to the existing Mark 10/11 source-destination confirmations, which only authorize a static outbound link.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A dated, explicit owner statement naming the exact source and the exact proposed automated behavior
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Owner interest expressed only informally, without a recorded, specific instruction naming the source and mechanism
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate if more than one site redesign or major architecture pass has occurred since authorization
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F0 does not authorize any route, component, fetch, or credential — it only records that evaluation may proceed.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Canonical source identifier supplied
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Confirms the exact technical identifier a real implementation would need (e.g. a channel ID, not a handle; an exact API endpoint; an exact feed URL) has been supplied by the owner directly, never derived, guessed, or resolved by search/scrape.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: The literal identifier string, supplied directly by the owner in a recorded, internal artifact
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Confusing a display handle with the actual technical identifier a feed mechanism requires
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredTechnicalRole: A reviewer confirms the identifier's format only (not a live reachability check — that is F4)
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate whenever the owner reports an account change, rename, or migration
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F1 does not authorize any network call to test the identifier — that is F4, a separate, later gate.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Source/account access and ownership evidence
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Confirms who actually controls the account/publication being proposed as a source, extending the existing Mark 8/8.1 source-verification-checklist model to cover automated-retrieval sources specifically.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: Same evidence categories as docs/internal/mark-8-tmm-source-verification-checklist.md — ownership/control evidence, not just an owner assertion of a handle
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Ownership evidence exists for the source-destination link (Mark 10/11) but was never extended to cover reproducing that account's raw feed/API output elsewhere
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F2 does not authorize display of any specific item pulled from that source — every item still needs its own G-M1 through G-M8.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Rights, attribution, and content-scope review
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Defines exactly which fields (title/date/excerpt/thumbnail/link) may ever be reproduced from this source, and under what attribution label, before any technical work begins.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A completed field-scoping decision — allowed fields, prohibited fields, attribution label, external-link policy (see Part D checklists)
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Treating 'the owner confirmed the source destination' (Mark 10/11) as equivalent to 'the owner confirmed which content fields may be reproduced' — these are different decisions
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredTechnicalRole: Editorial reviewer to flag any field likely to require special handling
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate if the source platform's terms or the owner's editorial policy changes
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F3 does not authorize retrieval or display of any specific content — only the field envelope.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Technical source retrieval proof
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: An isolated, out-of-band technical proof-of-concept, explicitly not part of this task, that the source can actually be retrieved in the proposed manner.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A documented, reproducible test showing successful retrieval, response shape, and any authentication/rate-limit behavior encountered
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Conflating a hypothesis with proof — this audit explicitly does not perform that proof
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredOwnerRole: None directly, but should review the proof's findings before proceeding
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredTechnicalRole: A technical reviewer, working in a separate, explicitly scoped task
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate if significant time passes before implementation begins, since third-party feed formats can change
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F4 does not authorize adding the fetch to this repository's build — that requires its own separate, source-specific implementation task plus F5-F8.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Build reliability, cache, timeout, and fallback proof
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Proves the proposed fetch cannot silently or loudly break a build, and that a failure degrades to the owner-hypothesized static fallback correctly, in both preview and production build modes.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A documented test showing build success under (a) source reachable, (b) source unreachable, (c) source slow/timing out, and consistent behavior across both PUBLIC_PREVIEW modes
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: No caching layer currently exists in this repository at all — this gate would be the first place a caching decision is actually implemented, not just proposed
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredOwnerRole: None directly, but should approve the fallback's exact visible wording
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate on any Astro version upgrade or build-tooling change
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F5 does not authorize a production release — that is still gated by the existing release-authorization process plus F8.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Privacy, tracking, and third-party-risk review
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Confirms the proposed source introduces no tracking, no unintended data exposure, and no change to the site's current zero-third-party-runtime-dependency posture without an explicit, documented decision to accept that change.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A written review confirming what a build-time fetch would expose to the third-party host and whether that is acceptable
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Assuming a 'public' feed has no privacy dimension — the build environment itself becomes a client making requests
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredOwnerRole: Owner sign-off on any residual risk
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate if the source's own privacy/data practices change or are newly discovered
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F6 does not authorize any analytics, tracking pixel, or cookie — those remain separately and independently prohibited by this repository's existing safeguards regardless of this gate.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Accessibility and editorial review
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: Confirms every field type proposed for display has a defined accessible treatment before any item using it is displayed, extending the same discipline already applied to the 8 existing destination cards (Mark 11).
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: A documented accessibility treatment per field type, and confirmation npm run test:a11y would still show 0 violations with the new field types present
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Free-text fields sourced from a third party are harder to guarantee accessible/appropriate than fully owner-authored card text
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate whenever a new field type is proposed for the same source
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F7 does not itself authorize display of any individual item — each item still needs its own G-M5 and full G-M1 through G-M8.

partC_feedSpecificGates.name: Owner final release authorization
partC_feedSpecificGates.purpose: The single, non-delegable final go/no-go for actually building the technical integration for this specific source — mirrors G-M8's role for individual media items, at the source/mechanism level.
partC_feedSpecificGates.evidenceRequired: An explicit, dated owner statement authorizing implementation of the specific mechanism proven under F4/F5, not just the source in general
partC_feedSpecificGates.commonBlockers: Treating F0 (initial hypothesis authorization) as equivalent to F8 (final build authorization)
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredOwnerRole: Owner only — may not be delegated
partC_feedSpecificGates.requiredTechnicalRole: None — an owner decision, informed by findings from F4-F7
partC_feedSpecificGates.expirationRevalidationRule: Revalidate if F1-F7 evidence exceeds a defined staleness window
partC_feedSpecificGates.note: Passing F8 still does not, by itself, authorize a new route, API, Worker, secret, deployment, or production release — each requires its own separate, explicitly scoped task.
